report:
PASS for the exact QEP-conditional theorem. The argument establishes actual realization, uniqueness modulo constants, and I-convergence of every normalized actual E1 maximizing sequence, for every fixed rational or irrational Reeb field on a cone satisfying the stated QEP antecedent. QEP is not established by this review. Original P13.2 remains open in its unconditional scope.

I used the task-granted P13.1, round73/76, and round79/81 mathematical bodies only within their accepted scopes. In particular, their universal root, topology, target-integrability, midpoint, and differentiation results supply no singular compactness or attainment. The new normal-quotient application supplies those steps under QEP; the earlier verdicts do not establish them.

The algebraic construction is valid on the original cone. The finitely many strict generator-weight inequalities define a nonempty rational open cone, so rational positive gradings exist. Clearing denominators and removing the supported degree gcd gives the effective grading. Normality of Proj follows on its degree-zero localization charts: an element of their fraction field integral over the degree-zero ring belongs to the normal localized graded ring and has degree zero. The resulting Y is integral and projective, of dimension p=n−1. A sufficiently divisible d supplies the actual ample invertible O_Y(d). For the existential theorem, eta and L_d must be chosen from the QEP witness. Sections of positive powers of this same L_d suffice for all FS constructions. If further divisibility is used, positive tensor scaling preserves EP through the corresponding PSH scaling.

Every calibration factor is retained: V_eta=s^(−n)d^(1−n)(L_d^p), omega=L_d/(sd), omega^p=sV_eta, and E_eta=E_Ld/(sd). The projective probability divides raw mixed curvature by (L_d^p). The radial calibration accounts for the difference between that projective mass and the affine-cone volume; neither denominator is substituted for the other.

The pertinent BJ statements and proofs have the required general-projective scope. Theorem 5.11 assumes irreducibility and EP, not smoothness or field countability. Its divisorial bounds, Tychonoff subnet, upper-tail envelopes, and genuine decreasing-limit closure produce an actual normalized PSH limit. Proposition 4.28 follows from finite divisorial detection for PL obstacles and uniform approximation of continuous obstacles. Theorem 7.1 and Proposition 7.7 give actual energy upper semicontinuity and decreasing-net continuity on the same singular variety. Thus QEP followed by 5.11 replaces the smooth EP input 5.20. [BJ v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

I also checked the supporting route to 9.19. Its signed-integration continuity comes from uniform approximation on bounded-J sets by model-MA pairings. The maximizing model outputs used there come from 9.11, which uses outer-energy differentiation, rather than inverse existence. The underlying relative-volume estimate has geometrically reduced projective scope; the actual normal Y over the retained perfect field meets that hypothesis. Neither this estimate nor BJ’s outer-energy statement imposes smoothness. The envelope-dependent inverse conclusions are unnecessary. [BJ v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4), [BGM Lemma 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.03847v1#page=12).

Residual torification preserves the actual bundle, its linearization, and its canonical reference. Splitting each section of a generating FS system into residual eigen-sections, keeping its coefficient, preserves global generation: simultaneous vanishing of all components would force simultaneous vanishing of the original sections. The Gauss maximum gives chi∘q, and the ultrametric inequality gives chi∘q≥chi. Uniform approximation and actual decreasing defining nets extend this calculation to CPSH and PSH. Composition with q commutes with every pointwise decreasing limit, including values −infinity. The trivial valuation is fixed, normalization is preserved, and energy monotonicity gives E_Ld(chi∘q)≥E_Ld(chi). Consequently actual E1 torifies to actual E1.

Both directions of the unbounded rational correspondence are justified. Cone defining nets lift to actual invariant projective CPSH nets; invariant projective potentials admit torified defining nets that lift back to actual cone CPSH nets. The correspondence preserves order and converges at every pertinent analytic point, not merely on divisorial points. The finite trivial-valuation value excludes an identically −infinity limit. Decreasing continuity of both energies extends E_eta=E_Ld/(sd), including energy −infinity, and hence identifies actual E1 in both directions. For E1 tuples, projective and cone weighted decreasing continuity extend the calibrated probabilities and weighted integrals. The limiting weight is integrable, support persists in the closed B and K, and the weighted identity retains 1/(sd). The energy-pairing expression is the test-containing pairing minus the zero-test pairing. These are fixed-eta statements.

The compactness map A is an actual normalized surjection. For the invariant lift Psi of a cone CPSH test, restriction to B and torification domination give exactly sup_Y(chi∘q−Psi)=sup_B(chi−Psi)=sup_Y(chi−Psi). Thus S_psi(A chi)=(sd)^(−1)sup_Y(chi−Psi). BJ 4.28 makes A continuous into the granted Hausdorff supremum-test topology. QEP compactness of its projective domain therefore proves actual cone compactness. No closure assertion about an invariant weak subset is needed.

The target lift has the required projective finite energy. The probability lambda_Y supported on B integrates every projective E1 potential chi: chi∘q is actual invariant E1, its cone restriction is actual E1, and chi=chi∘q on B. The granted cone integrability criterion therefore supplies projective integrability, and BJ 9.20 supplies finite projective dual energy on the original normal Y.

The whole-net L1 argument is valid. After restricting to the eventually bounded-J tail, cone energy upper semicontinuity puts u in actual E1. An alleged failure supplies a cofinal subnet with L1 distances bounded below. Its invariant projective lifts have J_Ld=sd J_eta and admit a weak further subnet under QEP. Energy upper semicontinuity makes its actual limit chi finite energy. Continuity of A and Hausdorffness identify A chi=u, without requiring chi to be invariant. BJ 9.19 then gives L1(lambda_Y) convergence. On B this is exactly sd times the cone distance, contradicting the alleged failure. It proves convergence of the entire original net.

All antecedents for the universal transfer are established. The finitely many positive generator ratios give finite a, b and delta. The actual root homeomorphism transfers normalized compactness. For bounded-J nets at xi, energy upper semicontinuity first makes the limit E1; inverse roots then give actual E1 nets at eta with bounded J by the accepted comparison. The accepted target criterion and root bounds identify the finite-energy target class on K. Every orbit pushforward is finite energy because |u(T_r x)−u(x)|≤2b|r| and the minus-infinity locus is preserved. The eta result supplies L1 convergence against the original target and every required rational orbit pushforward. The finite-grid lemma therefore applies: fix the finite grid before taking the net limit, refine its mesh, and send the unbounded cutoff to infinity last. Its tail estimate follows from source L1 convergence and the integrable fixed limit. Exceptional null sets are handled separately for each index and finite comparison. This establishes bounded-J target L1 continuity at every fixed xi without transporting MA between Reeb fields.

Attainment uses genuine H(xi) maximizing potentials. Their deficits tend to zero and the exact midpoint estimate gives J≤(L+d)/(2a_p), a_p=p/4^(p+1). Actual compactness gives a subnet limit; energy upper semicontinuity and target L1 continuity make it an actual E1 maximizer. The equality between the H and actual E1 dual suprema supplies the opposite variational inequality. The outer-obstacle inequality applies to w+tf because it is bounded above, usc, and target-integrable. Differentiation for both signs of t forces equality of target and actual fixed-xi MA integrals on the granted dense direction lattice. Positivity, Radon regularity, and mass one identify the two probabilities on K. The granted tangent identity proves necessity, and the embedding proves uniqueness modulo constants.

For any normalized actual E1 maximizing sequence, not only the H sequence used for existence, comparison with the attained maximizer gives I_xi(w_j,w)≤d_j/(2a_p)→0. This creates no completion element and requires no I-completeness assumption. For p=1 the bound is I≤8d. For n=1, the granted effective normal grading gives k[z], the one-point carrier, energy E(c)=c, and the calibrated radial probability; normalized potentials coincide and no a_0 estimate is used.

Harmless precisions and source corrections are explicit. Choose the rational data from the QEP witness, and interpret FS section systems as using powers of the actual L_d. The absolute-value identity is |a−b|=2(max(a,b)−b)−(a−b). Weighted integration uses the test-containing pairing minus the zero-test pairing. In the supporting polynomial estimates, the difference-of-powers telescope includes j=0 through p−1, and quadratic scaling uses t[1−(1−t)^p]≤pt^2. The elementary comparison in the printed 7.29 proof uses 1/4−x+x^2=(1/2−x)^2. These local corrections leave the stated estimates and interface proof intact.

Pending P16.1 arguments, reviews, and scalar descent supply no QEP premise here. Normality makes the proposed geometrically unibranch supplier applicable only if its exact EP theorem is independently established. The present acceptance remains conditional and does not close original P13.2.

passages.statement: Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Example 3.9, Theorems 4.5 and 4.15, Corollary 4.16, Definition 4.20 and Corollary 4.23: on an integral projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, with an ample line bundle L and its canonical trivial reference, actual PSH(c1(L)) potentials are precisely the nontrivial pointwise decreasing-net limits of FS potentials formed from sections of positive powers of this same L. Continuous PSH potentials are their uniform closure; nontrivial decreasing limits of PSH potentials remain PSH. Divisorial values determine potentials, and the weak topology is pointwise convergence on divisorial valuations.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Example 3.9, Theorems 4.5 and 4.15, Corollary 4.16, Definition 4.20 and Corollary 4.23: on an integral projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, with an ample line bundle L and its canonical trivial reference, actual PSH(c1(L)) potentials are precisely the nontrivial pointwise decreasing-net limits of FS potentials formed from sections of positive powers of this same L. Continuous PSH potentials are their uniform closure; nontrivial decreasing limits of PSH potentials remain PSH. Divisorial values determine potentials, and the weak topology is pointwise convergence on divisorial valuations.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 4.28: for an integral projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, an ample line bundle L, and every continuous real function gamma on Y^an, chi↦sup_Y^an(chi−gamma) is continuous on actual PSH(c1(L)) in the weak divisorial topology.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 5.11: for an irreducible projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and a numerical class theta, the envelope property for theta is equivalent to compactness of {chi∈PSH(theta): sup chi=0} in the weak divisorial topology. No smoothness or countability hypothesis is required.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 7.1 and Proposition 7.7: on an integral projective variety Y of dimension p over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, with ample L, the energy E_L(chi)=(L,chi)^(p+1)/((p+1)(L^p)) extends to actual PSH(c1(L)) by the infimum over dominating FS, equivalently continuous PSH, potentials. It is increasing, concave, weakly upper semicontinuous, satisfies E_L(chi+c)=E_L(chi)+c, and is continuous along decreasing nets, including limits of energy minus infinity.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 7.18 and Propositions 7.19 and 7.21: on an integral p-dimensional projective variety Y, p≥1, over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, with ample L, actual E1(L) tuples define positive Radon mixed curvature measures of raw mass (L^p). Model mixed measures have finite divisorial support, and every E1(L) potential is integrable against these mixed measures. Joint decreasing PSH nets with E1 limits give weak convergence of the mixed measures and their E1-weighted measures. For a limiting PSH weight outside E1, weighted convergence requires integrability against the limiting mixed measure.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 7.18 and Propositions 7.19 and 7.21: on an integral p-dimensional projective variety Y, p≥1, over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, with ample L, actual E1(L) tuples define positive Radon mixed curvature measures of raw mass (L^p). Model mixed measures have finite divisorial support, and every E1(L) potential is integrable against these mixed measures. Joint decreasing PSH nets with E1 limits give weak convergence of the mixed measures and their E1-weighted measures. For a limiting PSH weight outside E1, weighted convergence requires integrability against the limiting mixed measure.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 8.5: on an integral projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, with ample class omega, every chi∈E1(omega) and f∈PL(Y)_R satisfy E_omega^downarrow(chi+t f)=E_omega(chi)+t∫f dMA_omega(chi)+O_f(t^2) as t→0, with the error constant uniform in chi. This outer-energy statement requires neither smoothness nor the envelope property.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 9.19: on an integral projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, with ample L, if chi_i converges weakly to chi in actual PSH(c1(L)) and J_L(chi_i) is eventually bounded, then chi∈E1(L) and chi_i→chi in L1(lambda) for every Radon probability lambda of finite projective dual energy. Neither smoothness, the envelope property, nor inverse MA existence is an additional hypothesis.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 9.20: for an irreducible projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and ample L, a Radon probability lambda has finite dual energy sup_chi∈E1(L)(E_L(chi)−∫chi d lambda) if and only if every actual E1(L) potential belongs to L1(lambda). The envelope property is not required.

Boucksom–Gubler–Martin, arXiv:2004.03847v1, Lemma 3.2: let Y be a geometrically reduced projective scheme of dimension p≥1 over a complete non-Archimedean field, let L and M be ample line bundles, let phi be a continuous psh metric on L and psi_1,psi_2 continuous psh metrics on M. Set f=psi_1−psi_2 and C=((L+M)^p)−(L^p). With the relative-volume normalization vol(L,a,b)=lim_m p! m^(−p−1) log(det||·||_mb/det||·||_ma), one has C inf_Y^an f≤∫_Y^an f(dd^c phi+dd^c psi_1)^p−vol(L,phi+f,phi)≤C sup_Y^an f. No smoothness or envelope-property hypothesis is imposed.
